brief: Separate a regular commitment from a variable expense without assuming either is optional.

en-US.scenario: Fictional US-dollar examples for "Regular or variable?"; illustrative amounts, not current prices or product offers. No assumption of salary, bank ownership or spare income.

es-MX.scenario: Ejemplos ficticios en pesos mexicanos para "¿Regular o variable?"; montos ilustrativos, no precios vigentes ni ofertas. No se supone nómina, cuenta bancaria ni dinero sobrante.

pt-BR.scenario: Exemplos fictícios em reais para "Regular ou variável?"; valores ilustrativos, não preços atuais nem ofertas. Sem supor salário, conta bancária ou dinheiro sobrando.

objective.observable_action: Separate a regular commitment from a variable expense without assuming either is optional.
objective.success_criterion: Complete the fresh-context transfer using only its visible information.

instruction.relevance: Frequency and amount do not tell you whether an expense is optional.
instruction.misconception: Assuming every regular cost is essential and every changing expense is optional.
instruction.numeracy_support: The worked examples introduce the required operation; every assessed task retains its own amounts and assumptions.

evidence.reasoning: Rent repeats monthly; food spending changes with need. Both can be essential even though their amounts behave differently.
The payment repeats under the stated agreement.
The amount varies while the stated need remains.
Repeating charges do not prove an essential need.
Changing trip counts change cost without removing the stated need.
A recurring pattern can use an annual interval.
Necessity and consequences matter more than a fixed-versus-variable label.

delayed_retrieval.fresh_context: Retrieve this competence in the declared later course reviews and through the existing shared review system.
